svg.title: Transfer is demonstrated in use
svg.desc: A hypothetical delivery-planning team depends on Mina's judgment. Mina and Leo first capture the task's purpose, authoritative sources, checks, exceptions, and help routes in a short guide. Mina then demonstrates a real case and explains the clues behind her decisions. Leo leads the next run while Mina observes and gives feedback. A return arrow from practice to the guide shows how gaps in the instructions are corrected. Finally, Leo handles the agreed scope without prompting and escalates an unfamiliar case. This demonstrates usable coverage for a defined task, not replacement of all Mina's expertise. The number of steps is illustrative, not a prescribed training duration.

g.text: Hypothetical delivery-planning team · Documentation and practice work together
Only Mina knows how to resolve exceptions in the weekly delivery schedule.
Mina and Leo record the purpose, sources, checks, exceptions, and help routes.
A short, findable guide supports the task.
Mina works through a real case and explains the clues behind her choices.
Leo asks about decisions that the original instructions left implicit.
Leo leads the next run; Mina observes and gives feedback.
Gaps discovered in practice lead to corrections in the guide.
Leo handles the agreed scope without prompting and escalates an unfamiliar case.
Asking for the right help is part of competence.
Evidence of transfer: someone else can use the knowledge when needed.
Fictional people and sequence · Coverage of a defined task, not replacement of an expert
Training time and supervision depend on the task, learner, and consequences of mistakes.
